title: Find the letter on the panel, write its neighbour: search-and-step through 50 readings of the carved texts, 30 offsets, 5 pointer rules, every start cell, in both roles (decoder searches the K4 letter; encoder searches the plain letter)
k4_result: Forward role (go to the next cell holding the K4 letter, read the cell at the offset): 11,451,060 settings give 515,953 different 97-letter readings (the walks merge after the first letter). Best 8 of 24 clue letters in place (159 settings, all one family: K1-K3 plaintext in the carved cells read by columns backwards, pointer reset at each carved row, 3 cells to the left); 24 needed; none at 9. Mean 1.16 of 24. Best per pointer rule: same 6, next 7, one-on 6, row-reset 8, jump 7. The 8/24 readings are gibberish (big model -7.08, word cover 0.09). Most English-looking reading that is not a straight copy of a panel: -5.96, word cover 0.31, 3/24 clue letters (English needs about -5.1). BERLIN, CLOCK, NORTHEAST, EASTNORTH appear nowhere in any reading. Reverse role (encoder searches the plain letter, carves the neighbour; each clue word walked exactly from every pointer, the two words not even required to link): 11,451,060 settings, best 9 of 24 (5 of 13 + 4 of 11, one setting); 24 needed, so nothing reached the full decode.
controls: 40 shuffled K4s, identical run (the shuffled text also replaces K4 in the panels that hold K4). Forward best clue letters: 6 (7 shuffles), 7 (26), 8 (6), 9 (1); 7 of 40 are at or above K4's 8. Best non-copy English: -6.30 to -5.62, median -6.02; 12 of 40 are at or above K4's -5.96. Reverse best: 7 (6), 8 (19), 9 (15); 15 of 40 at or above K4's 9. Copies set aside: 142-1075 per shuffle (K4 695). K4 is inside the controls on every count.
planted: 7/7. Forward role 4/4 found at 24/24 at the planted panel, order, offset, pointer rule and start and read back 97/97 (cipher panel rows with the east-north-east offset (-1,+2), pointer 'next'; K1-K3 plaintext right-aligned rows backwards, one row down, row-reset; K1-K3 plaintext by columns, one cell left with holes, jump; tableau by columns, one cell right, 'same', ordinary English). Reverse role 3/3: planted setting among the 3-16 settings at 24/24, and the beam decode with the clue letters gave 96, 96 and 97 of 97 letters (big model -3.83 to -4.19).
scope_limits: Reference texts: the two panels as transcribed in data/sculpture_layout.json (cipher panel K1-K3 cells only and all 28 rows; K1-K3 plaintext as carved, misspellings kept, in the cells of its ciphertext, alone and followed by K4; tableau panel 28 rows and its 26-row body) and the 81-letter Morse text. Rows left- or right-aligned only: the real copper has uneven letter spacing, so 'the cell above' may differ from both. Reading orders: rows, columns, both backwards (no back-and-forth, no diagonals, no spirals). Offsets: 1-3 cells left/right, 1-3 rows up/down, 8 knight steps, 4 diagonal neighbours, 1-3 places along the reading order; one fixed offset for the whole message. Pointer rules: same, next, one-on, row-reset, jump to the neighbour; the search always runs forwards along the reading order and wraps. Not covered: an offset that changes per letter or per row, the letter found in one panel and the neighbour taken from the other panel (the two sides of the sculpture), searching for pairs of letters, K2 with the corrected ending, any transposition or substitution before or after. Reverse role: counted on the clue words with free pointers (an upper bound); the full decode was built and passes its plants but had no K4 setting to run on. Forward plants on the cipher panel and the plaintext grid use strings of common English words chosen so the encoder never gets stuck, because ordinary prose cannot be written that way (see outcome). Clue positions taken as exact.

negative.hypothesis: K4 is read by keeping a finger on a carved panel: move on to the next place where the K4 letter (or, for the encoder, the plain letter) occurs and take the letter at a fixed offset from it, such as one step east-north-east.
negative.scope: 50 texts (cipher panel with and without K4, K1-K3 plaintext in the carved cells with and without K4, tableau panel and body, Morse; left/right aligned; rows, columns, both backwards) x 30 offsets (left/right and up/down 1-3, knight steps, diagonals, 1-3 along the reading order) x 2 edge rules x 5 pointer rules (same, next, one-on, reset at carved K4 rows, jump to neighbour) x every start cell: 11,451,060 settings read in full in the forward role and the same number tested exactly on the clue words in the reverse role.
negative.outcome: Dead: forward best 8/24 clue letters and best English -5.96 (needs -5.1); reverse best 9/24; 24 needed (controls: 40 shuffled K4s give forward 6-9, English -6.30 to -5.62, reverse 7-9; 7, 12 and 15 of 40 at or above K4; planted 7/7). Also: in the forward role ordinary English cannot be encoded on the cipher panel (0 of 200 messages, half stuck within 10-11 letters) and almost never on the K1-K3 plaintext (0-2 of 200); in the reverse role the ciphertext is never as flat as K4 (IC 0.050-0.054 on the cipher panel, lowest 0.038 in 800 messages, K4 0.0361; 0.064-0.067 on plaintext and tableau).

follow_ups: Two-sided version: find the letter on the cipher panel, take the letter at the same row and cell (or mirrored cell) of the tableau panel on the other side of the copper, and the reverse. Needs only the two transcribed panels; the row/cell alignment of the two sides is the free parameter (shifts of 0-3 cells, mirrored or not).
